subject: Operational safeguards & renewal: escalated SLA proposal for Atlas Bank
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@atlasbank.com
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas — recurring tail-latency spikes impacting payments; renewal at risk

Hi Rishi,

I wanted to escalate: over the past 6 weeks we've seen recurring tail-latency spikes during end-of-day batch clearings. The attached CSV shows multiple 95th/99th percentile spikes correlated with our largest settlement windows. These spikes are causing delayed payment acknowledgements and manual interventions.

We're approaching renewal and this is now a commercial risk — our internal stakeholders are asking for concrete operational safeguards (guarantees on tail latency and an escalation pathway).

Can Redwood propose an operational mitigation and a path to (a) immediate remediation for the next two settlement cycles and (b) a commercial/contractual assurance (SLA amendment or premium offering) that prevents future regressions? We need to see a concrete pilot plan and proposed credits if SLOs are missed.

Samira
Head of Payments Engineering
Atlas Bank

Attachments: atlas_latency_report_Q4.csv (CSV, 24KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-05T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas — recurring tail-latency spikes impacting payments; renewal at risk

Samira — thank you for the detailed report and for flagging the renewal timeline. I'm sorry to hear the spikes are impacting settlement workflows.

Quick plan:
- Can we schedule a short triage (30 min) tomorrow to walk the CSV with your SREs?
- Internally, I'll spin up a temporary priority routing + dedicated micro-pool for your peak windows for the next two settlement cycles as an interim mitigation.
- We'll propose a formal "Enterprise Resilience" amendment that includes a tail-latency SLO (99th percentile at X ms) and a credit structure for misses.

I've looped in Monica (Customer Success) and Neha (Reliability) to prepare a pilot configuration and uplift proposal. We'll come prepared with a timeline and expected improvements.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Team — Samira from Atlas sent over the latency report (attached by customer). Renewal is imminent; they see tail spikes that impact settlement. High-level asks: immediate mitigation for next two cycles + a contractual assurance (SLA upgrade or premium tier).

Proposed commercial/operational response:
- Offer a 30-day pilot: dedicated micro-pool for their peak settlement windows + prefix/KV caching tuned to their workload.
- Formal amendment: "Enterprise Resilience Tier" with a 99.95% availability target and a 99th/99.9th tail-latency SLO for API responses during settlement windows. Missed SLOs -> financial credit formula (sliding scale).
- Offer 1 month of pro-rated credits if we fail any scheduled settlement window during pilot.

Action items:
- Neha: run a root-cause analysis and provide a short mitigation runbook + expected % reduction in 99th/99.9th latency. Include whether kernel changes or GC tuning needed. Also capture telemetry links.
- Monica: draft the pilot commercial summary and impact on renewal pricing; include conditional credit language.
- Marcus: draft an amendment and a one-page exec summary for Samira's CFO.

Attachments for internal: redwood-proposed-resilience-pilot-ATLAS-20261206.pdf

Thanks,
Rishi

Date: 2026-12-07T14:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Atlas escalation — technical summary and recommended steps

Quick TL;DR from infra: we see periodic KV-cache thrash and increased contention on our routing layer when Atlas bursts overlap with other customers' batch work. Root causes and mitigations: 

- Observed behavior: 99th-percentile jumps from ~120ms to 1.2s during peak windows; 99.9th spikes up to 2.6s. Spikes line up with their 02:00–03:00 UTC settlement windows.
- Short-term mitigations (48–72 hrs): priority routing for Atlas requests during their settlement windows + pre-warm KV caches for their top 200 prefixes; limit cross-tenant opportunistic batching during the window. Expected impact: reduce 99th to ~180–220ms, 99.9th to ~350–550ms (empirical estimate).
- Medium-term (pilot): dedicated micro-pool with reserved capacity, tuned kernel flags, and a canary rollout of the prefix cache improvements. Expected impact: 99th < 150ms, 99.9th < 250ms for settlement windows.
- Telemetry: uploaded sampled traces for their window to internal link: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/atlas/trace-sample-20261207 (internal).
- Risks: if their peaks grow beyond current committed concurrency, we'll need to scale the micro-pool; cost will move to reserved capacity.

I'll prepare a concise runbook and a short JIRA ticket set to implement the priority routing and cache pre-warm.

-Neha
Principal Reliability Engineer

Subject: Formal proposal: Enterprise Resilience pilot and SLA amendment (Atlas Bank)

Samira — thanks again for the discussion earlier this week. Based on Neha's analysis, here's our formal proposal to address your concerns and to provide contractual assurance ahead of renewal: 

Executive summary:
- 30-day pilot covering the next two settlement cycles (dates: 2026-12-20 and 2026-12-27). Pilot includes: dedicated micro-pool reserved for Atlas during 02:00–04:00 UTC windows, prefix/KV pre-warm, and priority routing.
- SLOs for settlement windows: 99th percentile API latency <= 150ms; 99.9th <= 250ms.
- Contract: optional amendment to add "Enterprise Resilience Tier" to your contract. If pilot fails to meet SLOs, Redwood will issue pro-rated credits and an additional month of premium support at no cost.
- Pricing/credits: attached one-page commercial offer; pricing assumes reserved micro-pool for settlement windows.
- Timeline: kickoff 2026-12-15 (implementation and canary), pilot 2026-12-20 through 2026-12-27, checkpoint 2026-12-28.

Next steps we propose:
1) Samira: confirm pilot kickoff and confirm who from Atlas will be on the daily checkpoint calls.
2) Procurement loop: we'll route amendment and DocuSign link to procurement once Atlas signs off on scope.
3) Neha: we'll publish the runbook and telemetry access for Atlas.

Attachments: redwood-enterprise-resilience-offer-ATLAS-20261208.pdf
DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ATLAS/DocuSignEnvelopeId/1234567890

If this looks good I'll have Marcus draft the formal amendment and Monica will coordinate kickoff.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
